capability: multi-layer caching with write-through support and namespace isolation
use_when: you need to cache data with priority-ordered layers, write-through persistence, or namespace-separated cache regions

capability: database connection pooling with read/write splitting for MySQL, PostgreSQL, and SQLite
use_when: you need managed database connections, a connection pool, or read/write endpoint splitting

capability: in-process event dispatching with priority ordering, type-hierarchy matching, and stoppable events
use_when: you need to publish or listen to domain events within a single process
alternatives: for cross-process or queued event delivery use jardisadapter/messaging instead

capability: unified filesystem abstraction for local and S3 storage with stream support and visibility control
use_when: you need to read, write, delete, or stream files across local or cloud storage backends

capability: outbound HTTP client with a composable middleware pipeline, automatic retry, and cURL transport
use_when: you need to make outbound HTTP requests with configurable middleware, retry logic, or a custom transport

capability: structured logging with multiple output handlers, contextual enrichment, and level-based routing
use_when: you need application logging that routes records to multiple targets or enriches them with contextual metadata

capability: SMTP mailer with STARTTLS, HTML and plain-text bodies, attachments, retry, and persistent keepalive
use_when: you need to send transactional or notification emails via SMTP

capability: multi-transport asynchronous messaging with publish/consume support for Redis, Kafka, RabbitMQ, Database, and in-memory
use_when: you need asynchronous message passing, event streaming, or queue-based communication between bounded contexts
alternatives: for synchronous, in-process domain events use jardisadapter/eventdispatcher instead

capability: HTTP delivery layer for Jardis-generated domains — a FastRoute router behind its own RouterInterface, a PSR-15 middleware pipeline (global and per-route, ready-made RequireSession), and the canonical DomainResponse-to-PSR-7 envelope mapper
use_when: you need to expose a Jardis-generated domain's read-facades/process()/rules over HTTP, with routing, PSR-15 middleware, and a ready-made {status,data,errors,meta} response envelope

capability: immutable infrastructure holder (the DomainKernel) for Jardis-generated domains, with an optional ENV-driven bootstrap packer that also assembles the ready-made session and token services from configuration
use_when: you need to assemble and inject the infrastructure (db connection, cache, logger, events, HTTP client, mailer, filesystem, session and token services) that a generated {Domain} facade takes via constructor injection

capability: session management with signed access tokens (no database access per request) that carry subject, tenant and role, password hashing and authentication, a ready-made bundle of session and token services (also available through the kernel), and role-based access control with domain events
use_when: you need user login, session lifecycle management, password verification, or role-based permission checks

capability: versioned class resolution via namespace injection with proxy caching and fallback chain
use_when: you need to load domain classes by version, resolve namespace-based variants, or support backward-compatible class loading

capability: shared port interfaces and contracts for all Jardis packages, including the authentication, token and session-service ports
use_when: you need the interface definitions that Jardis adapters implement, without depending on any concrete implementation

capability: entity hydration from raw data, change tracking, field mapping with optional skipping of null values for write-only columns, and unique identifier generation
use_when: you need to hydrate domain entities from persistence data, detect changed fields, map column names, or generate unique entity identifiers

capability: fluent SQL query builder for SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, CTEs, and window functions
use_when: you need to build SQL queries programmatically without a full ORM, or construct complex queries with CTEs or window functions
alternatives: for standard entity CRUD with a repository abstraction use jardissupport/repository instead

capability: .env file loading with type casting, variable substitution, cascade loading, and optional secret integration
use_when: you need to load and manage environment configuration from .env files with type safety or multi-file cascade
alternatives: for AES-256 encrypted secrets stored alongside .env values use jardissupport/secret in addition

capability: dependency injection container with reflection-based instantiation and optional backend container delegation
use_when: you need to resolve and wire service dependencies automatically without manual constructor calls

capability: generic CRUD repository with raw-data persistence, read/write endpoint splitting, and flexible primary-key strategies
use_when: you need a data-access layer for persisting and retrieving domain entities with built-in read/write splitting
alternatives: for custom or complex SQL queries use jardissupport/dbquery instead

capability: the answer of one request-response use case in one shape: response objects, failure forms for 400/404/409/422, the data of the `{status, data, errors, meta}` envelope, read answers (`ReadResult`, `Reference`) and the door steps in front of a use case (input check, mapping of thrown failures, logging of the 5xx cause)
use_when: you need to build, map or log the answer of a request-response use case, or a Jardis-style failure form and response envelope, without a process engine
alternatives: to run a node graph use jardissupport/workflow; for transactions use jardissupport/repository

capability: cron expression parsing, task definition with tags and priority, and schedule validation
use_when: you need to define, parse, validate, or manage recurring scheduled tasks and cron-based job configurations

capability: encrypted secret resolution from .env files using AES-256-GCM and Sodium
use_when: you need to store and resolve encrypted credentials or secrets in environment files with strong cryptographic protection

capability: composable object-graph validation with composite validators, field-level rules, and a fluent builder API
use_when: you need to validate domain objects, input data, or value objects with chainable, reusable validation rules

capability: process engine for one request-response use case: node graph, routes, typed outcome (no door, no transaction)
use_when: you need to declare and run a multi-node use case with routes; the transaction around it is the door's (jardissupport/repository)
alternatives: the answer, failure forms and door steps live in jardissupport/response
